vibe: OpenAI's messy divorce from Cursor and a fresh Anthropic copyright lawsuit carry the AI beat today, while a Claude Code prompt-injection trick and a wave of WordPress RCEs are the actual patch-and-be-careful items.

cyber.title: Researcher shows how Claude Code can be tricked simply by asking it to summarize a website
cyber.summary: A security researcher demonstrated that Claude Code can be steered into unintended actions just by asking it to summarize a malicious website — hidden instructions in the page content get treated as if they came from the user. Straightforward prompt-injection risk for anyone using Claude Code's web-fetch/browsing features, worth reading given how often you're driving Claude Code day to day.

cyber.title: Five Critical WordPress Plugin and Theme Flaws Enable Site Takeover or RCE
cyber.summary: Five newly disclosed critical flaws across popular WordPress plugins and themes allow full site takeover or remote code execution. Classic mass-scan bait — patch immediately if you or anyone you know self-hosts WordPress.

cyber.title: McKesson discloses breach after ShinyHunters claims patient data theft
cyber.summary: Healthcare/pharma giant McKesson disclosed a breach after extortion group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen patient data — another entry in ShinyHunters' ongoing run against major US firms this year.

cyber.title: The Cybersecurity Apocalypse Is Coming in 'Months,' AI Giants Warn
cyber.summary: Wired rounds up warnings from multiple AI labs that AI-accelerated offense — automated vulnerability discovery plus exploit writing — could produce a step change in attack volume within months. More a temperature check than a single incident, but notable that it's coming from the people building the models.

cyber.title: IBM Langflow OSS hit with five high-severity CVEs: auth bypass, path traversal, RCE, SSRF
cyber.summary: Langflow, a popular open-source agent-building framework, picked up five high-severity CVEs in one disclosure batch — a namespace-collision info leak, a path-traversal file read, an improper-authentication flow-execution bug, arbitrary code execution via flow definitions, and SSRF. If you're experimenting with Langflow, update before exposing an instance to anything untrusted.

cyber.title: Just a rumour of a bug is enough to find a security exploit these days
cyber.summary: Willison writes up a case where a mere rumour that a bug existed was enough for someone to go find and weaponize a real one — a neat illustration of how AI-assisted research is closing the gap between 'someone mentioned a bug' and 'someone has a working exploit.'

cyber.title: Cosmos EVM Flaw Exploited After Cosmos Labs Knew Every Blockchain Running It Was Vulnerable
cyber.summary: An EVM-compatibility flaw across Cosmos-based blockchains got exploited after Cosmos Labs reportedly already knew every chain running the vulnerable code was exposed — a patching/governance failure as much as a technical one.

ai.title: OpenAI will pull its models from Cursor due to SpaceXAI acquisition
ai.summary: OpenAI is cutting off Cursor's access to its models after Cursor's acquisition by Elon Musk's SpaceX/xAI, publishing its own blog post to explain the call — seeing a competitor now own a popular AI coding tool was an unacceptable conflict. Big shakeup for anyone running Cursor on GPT models; expect a scramble to Claude or Gemini backends. Confirmed by CNBC and OpenAI's own post (770+ points on HN).

ai.title: Sony Music and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
ai.summary: Sony Music and Warner Chappell filed a copyright suit accusing Anthropic of a 'brazen campaign' of IP theft in training its models — the highest-profile music-industry suit yet against an AI lab, landing right as Anthropic is reportedly prepping an IPO. Also covered by Engadget and TechCrunch.

ai.title: Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude
ai.summary: AI-terminal company Warp details how it built agents on Claude that iteratively improve their own prompts and tool use from real usage data — a solid engineering write-up if you're building anything agentic on top of Claude.

ai.title: I accidentally turned LLM memory into program analysis
ai.summary: A researcher describes stumbling into a genuinely new program-analysis technique while building memory systems for LLM agents. Niche but well-regarded on HN (260+ points) — worth a skim if you like the security-research/agent-tooling intersection.

ai.title: Tencent Releases and Open-Sources Tencent Hy4 Preview
ai.summary: Tencent released and open-sourced a preview of its latest model, Hy4 — light on independent coverage so far, but another entrant in the crowded open-weight race out of China.

ai.title: StemDeck, a free, open-source and local AI stem separator
ai.summary: A fully local, open-source AI tool for splitting songs into vocals/instrument stems landed on HN with strong traction — handy if you want to pull stems without a cloud subscription.

it.title: AWS mumbles about its cost-busting networking tech when it should be shouting
it.summary: The Register argues AWS has quietly shipped meaningful networking cost reductions but has done a poor job publicizing them — worth a look if you're doing any AWS network-cost optimization work.

it.title: Nvidia's AI advantage is moving beyond the GPU
it.summary: Analysis piece on how Nvidia's moat is shifting from raw chip performance toward the surrounding software/networking stack (CUDA, NVLink) plus its growing string of strategic AI-company investments.

videos.title: The Only Way to Fund Open Source Is to Sell It
videos.verdict: SKIM — it's a rambling ~2hr livestream (hosts catching up after weeks off, lots of personal chat) but the segment on the rumored Nvidia/Hugging Face acquisition and Stripe's purchase of OpenRouter is worth 10 minutes. Their thesis: at current AI-infrastructure valuations, open-source projects can't sustain themselves on donations or usage fees, so the only realistic exit is being bought by a strategically-motivated player (Nvidia wanting AI to not consolidate around 2-3 closed labs). Skip the first 15-20 minutes of catch-up chat and jump straight to the Hugging Face/Nvidia discussion.
videos.summary: Live-show discussion arguing that at current AI-infrastructure valuations, open-source projects like Hugging Face and OpenRouter can only survive by being acquired by a strategically-motivated buyer rather than through direct monetization.
